I had an issue where git wasn't ignoring files listed in .gitignore. Apparently, if the files were accidentally committed before they were added to the .gitignore file, Git still tracks them. I found a python script that permanently purges ignored files using the filter-repo command. Unfortunately, the script doesn't appear to work. When I first ran it, it listed all the ignored files and asked for confirmation to delete them. It claimed to delete them, but whenever I rerun it on the same repo it lists the same files it claimed to have previously deleted. They also show up during staging when those files are regenerated. What gives? #!/usr/bin/env python3 import os import subprocess import sys import pathspec def get_current_origin(target_dir): """Safely retrieves the remote origin URL if it exists.""" try: result = subprocess.run( ["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"], check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, cwd=target_dir ) return result.stdout.strip() except subprocess.CalledProcessError: return None # No remote origin configuration set up def get_ignored_paths(target_dir): gitignore_path = os.path.join(target_dir, '.gitignore') if not os.path.exists(gitignore_path): print(f"Error: No .gitignore file found in {target_dir}") sys.exit(1) with open(gitignore_path, 'r') as f: lines = f.read().splitlines() spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines('gitwildmatch', lines) ignored_paths = [] for root, dirs, files in os.walk(target_dir): if '.git' in dirs: dirs.remove('.git') for name in files + dirs: full_path = os.path.join(root, name) rel_path = os.path.relpath(full_path, target_dir) if rel_path == '.': continue if spec.match_file(rel_path): if os.path.isdir(full_path) and not rel_path.endswith('/'): rel_path += '/' ignored_paths.append(rel_path) return sorted(list(set(ignored_paths))) def run_filter_repo(): if len(sys.argv) < 2: print("Usage: ./purge_external.py /path/to/your/git/project") sys.exit(1) target_dir = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1]) if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(target_dir, '.git')): print(f"Error: {target_dir} is not a valid Git repository.") sys.exit(1) paths_to_remove = get_ignored_paths(target_dir) if not paths_to_remove: print("No files or folders currently found matching your .gitignore rules.") return # STEP 1: Grab the remote origin URL before git-filter-repo destroys it origin_url = get_current_origin(target_dir) print(f"Target Project: {target_dir}") if origin_url: print(f"Detected Remote Origin: {origin_url}") print("
The following paths match your .gitignore and will be PERMANENTLY deleted from history:") for p in paths_to_remove: print(f" - {p}") confirm = input("
Are you absolutely sure you want to purge these? (yes/no): ") if confirm.lower() != 'yes': print("Operation cancelled.") return # STEP 2: Execute git-filter-repo with the --force flag included cmd = ["git", "filter-repo", "--invert-paths", "--force"] for path in paths_to_remove: cmd.extend(["--path", path]) print("
Running git-filter-repo...") try: subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, cwd=target_dir) print("Success! History rewritten locally.") # STEP 3: Automatically rebuild and restore the origin remote configuration if origin_url: print(f"Restoring remote origin connection to: {origin_url}") subprocess.run(["git", "remote", "add", "origin", origin_url], check=True, cwd=target_dir) print("Origin successfully restored.") print("
👉 Next Step: Run 'git push origin --force --all' to sync changes with your remote server.") else: print("
No remote origin was set up previously. No restoration needed.") except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e: print(f"
Error encountered during execution: {e}") if __name__ == "__main__": run_filter_repo()
